claims.statement: DOE guidance says compressed-air leaks can waste 20-30% of compressor output, but this is a general upper-range industrial benchmark rather than evidence of a profitable leak backlog at any Polish target plant.

DOE guidance says one-time leak repair is insufficient: a leak-prevention program should include identification, tagging, tracking, repair, verification and employee involvement, and compressor controls must be adjusted after repair for the reduced demand to translate into energy savings.

An Atlas Copco case reports that an industrial customer used flow, pressure and leak measurements, then repaired the most serious leaks itself; the reported result was 301,000 kWh annual reduction, EUR 9,000 annual savings and repair payback below four months. The vendor case neither identifies a Polish plant nor discloses an audit price or savings-share payment.

DB Energy reports an unnamed construction-sector compressed-air audit-and-repair project with PLN 170,000 investment, 2.21 GWh annual savings, PLN 574,600 annual cost reduction and payback below six months. This is provider-controlled evidence and does not disclose the service provider's price, margin, acquisition cost or performance-fee structure.

Article 11 of Directive (EU) 2023/1791 tells Member States to ensure that enterprises averaging more than 10 TJ of annual energy consumption across all carriers over the prior three years, without an energy-management system, complete a first audit by 11 October 2026; the 85 TJ group must implement a certified energy-management system by 11 October 2027.

The operative consolidated Polish Energy Efficiency Act surfaced in ELI requires an enterprise audit every four years from entrepreneurs other than micro, small and medium-sized entrepreneurs; its Article 36 does not state the Directive's 10 TJ threshold or 11 October 2026 deadline.

The claimed near-term Polish compliance trigger is not established by the cited EU rule alone: the Directive directs Member States, while the operative consolidated Polish statute located for this research still expresses a size-based obligation. Exact Polish applicability of the 10 TJ deadline therefore requires confirmation against any later implementing amendment or regulator guidance before it can support acquisition forecasts.

Under Article 36(3) of the Polish Act, a statutory enterprise audit may be conducted by an independent entity with knowledge and professional experience or by an internal expert not directly involved in the audited activity; the text does not impose a named accreditation or registry requirement.

The Polish Act requires the statutory enterprise audit to review buildings, industrial installations and transport representing at least 90% of the enterprise's total energy consumption, so a compressed-air-only survey cannot automatically satisfy the statutory audit and is at most a workstream within a broader audit unless that system alone meets the coverage rule.

EU law recognizes energy-performance contracting in principle as a verified and monitored arrangement where works, supply or services are paid relative to an agreed efficiency improvement or financial savings criterion.

Annex XV of Directive (EU) 2023/1791 requires energy-performance contracts to address guaranteed savings, duration and milestones, each party's duties, reference dates, implementation steps and costs, full implementation and change documentation, subcontracting, division of monetary savings, measurement and verification, changed energy prices or installation intensity, and breach penalties.

IPMVP states that savings cannot be measured directly and must be determined from before-and-after consumption with adjustments. It specifically calls for treatment of new production shifts and operating-hour changes, utility-price rules, meter accuracy and calibration, data responsibilities, uncertainty, quality assurance, and a budget for initial and ongoing M&V work.

The Polish Ministry of Climate and Environment publishes a directory of established ESCO providers and says entry requires evidence of at least one completed ESCO-formula project. The directory includes multiple industrial energy-service firms and explicitly lists E.ON Polska Solutions for compressed air, industrial installations, construction, service, remote management and technical analysis.

Festo Poland already offers a manufacturer-independent, in-operation compressed-air audit spanning generation, preparation, distribution and pneumatic applications, with leak location, savings assessment, prioritized repairs, an ISO 11011-aligned certificate and ISO 50001 support.

Festo's one-year subscription portal already captures on-site compressed-air efficiency measures, quantifies losses, costs and savings, manages repair and spare-parts workflows, stores projects for cross-period and cross-plant comparison, and lets customers decide read/write access.

Atlas Copco Poland's AIRScan service already installs measurement tools during operation, measures energy, flow and pressure, detects and prioritizes leaks, provides an ISO 11011-aligned report, offers a repair method, and connects the audit to continuous SMARTLINK monitoring and compressor controls.

The Atlas case establishes that at least one industrial customer requested an incumbent compressed-air assessment and acted on its repair plan, but it does not establish that the customer paid for the audit, accepted a performance fee, renewed monitoring, or resembles the proposed Polish target segment.

URE reports a 2025 average competitive wholesale-market electricity sale price of PLN 458.24/MWh. The notice covers transactions by generators and trading companies, not a target plant's delivered tariff, demand charges, taxes or avoided marginal cost, so it cannot by itself price plant savings.

No primary evidence was found that a Polish manufacturing buyer will pay the proposed PLN 12,000-25,000 initial survey fee plus 20-30% of independently verified first-year compressed-air savings, or that procurement will accept this hybrid price instead of a fixed-fee incumbent audit.

Fully loaded contribution economics remain unknown because there are no validated quotes or operating data for Polish field labor, travel, metering and calibration, safety training, insurance, legal and M&V work, partner share, sales effort, customer repair completion, collection delay, warranty exposure, support or re-survey cost.

No accredited auditor, compressor-service firm, distributor or other channel has provided a letter of intent, referral terms, customer access, field capacity, non-compete boundary or cost schedule for the proposed venture.

Before an executed agreement, the venture cannot unilaterally control the proposed critical control point: a plant must grant site, meter and operational-data access and accept repair, baseline and M&V duties, while an incumbent portal explicitly leaves access control with the customer. A durable position can only be acquired contractually and none is presently evidenced.

Delivery is materially dependent on customer or partner field action: authoritative guidance requires recurring detection, repair, verification and compressor-control adjustment, and the available project cases realize savings only after physical repairs. Without a committed field-and-repair partner, this is not a data-science-only service executable by the founder in five hours per day.

A defensible data moat is not currently evidenced: government-listed ESCOs already occupy industrial efficiency relationships, and Festo and Atlas already use proprietary measurement software, repeat-project data, monitoring, repair workflows and ISO-aligned reports. Site data also remains customer-controlled unless contract rights say otherwise.

contrary_evidence: The EU 10 TJ deadline is an instruction to Member States, while the operative consolidated Polish statute located for this research still states a size-based audit obligation; the proposed October 2026 Polish buying trigger is therefore not yet grounded in confirmed domestic implementation.

The Polish statutory enterprise audit must cover at least 90% of total enterprise energy use, so a compressed-air survey does not automatically discharge the compliance obligation that is supposed to trigger purchase.

The Polish Ministry's ESCO directory already contains numerous industrial energy-service providers, explicitly including E.ON Polska Solutions for compressed air, and the directory requires at least one completed ESCO project for entry.

Festo Poland and Atlas Copco Poland already offer much of the proposed workflow: in-operation metering, leak detection and prioritization, repair documentation, ISO-aligned reporting, monitoring software and parts or service integration.

IPMVP and EU contract requirements make shared-savings attribution a continuing contractual and operational process involving baseline adjustments, changed production conditions, data custody, meter quality, reporting resources and breach allocation.

DOE guidance and the available vendor cases show that physical repairs and compressor-control changes, not the survey alone, cause savings; customer delay or refusal can eliminate performance-fee revenue.

Published waste percentages and selected vendor success cases do not establish target-site backlog, Polish willingness to pay the proposed price, repeat purchase, sales-cycle length or venture contribution margin.

unknowns: Whether a later Polish implementing amendment or binding regulator guidance makes the Directive's 10 TJ threshold and 11 October 2026 deadline directly operative for the intended private-enterprise segment.

How many reachable Polish manufacturing plants have material compressed-air loads, no current audit or monitoring relationship, a repair-ready leak backlog and authority to sign a savings-sharing contract.
Whether any target buyer accepts PLN 12,000-25,000 upfront plus a 20-30% share of verified first-year savings and the proposed 12-24 month baseline and verification term.
Whether plants will grant timely site, meter, tariff, production and maintenance data access and accept a pre-agreed method for routine and non-routine baseline adjustments.
The percentage of identified leaks customers actually repair, time to repair, persistence of repairs, compressor-control changes after repair and collectability of contingent fees.
Auditor and field-service partner willingness, referral ownership, non-compete restrictions, capacity, safety credentials, service-level commitments and economic terms.
Fully loaded acquisition, travel, survey, metering, calibration, insurance, legal, reporting, support, remeasurement and dispute-resolution costs per site.
Sales-cycle duration, initial-survey conversion, multi-site expansion, renewal frequency and churn under a shared-savings model.
Whether plant contracts can grant durable, transferable rights to longitudinal leak, repair and savings data sufficient to create an advantage over incumbent OEM and ESCO datasets.
